newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ruling party under fire on Communist funds.
newsitem.headline: Polish ruling party under fire on Communist funds.

text.p: Poland's ruling Social Democrats were accused on Thursday of hanging onto pre-1989 Communist party assets which courts have ruled belong to the state.
Opposition member of parliament Jacek Taylor told private Radio Zet that some prominent Social Democrats were trying to block court decisions on the Communist Party's once vast funds and property.

"These people have lost the right to occupy state positions," Taylor said, appealing to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz -- a former communist but not a member of the Social Democrats -- to intervene.

The row stems from the dismissal on Wednesday of Marek Biernacki, who was appointed to recover party assets by a previous government and has carried on his dogged battle to since the ex-communists won power in 1993 elections.
His sacking, by the Social Democrat governor of Gdansk, took place as he was pressing a court case to force the Social Democrats to open their accounts.

Many of the Communists' assets have been transferred but the Social Democrat Party argued it had the right to keep those which came from members' contributions or were needed to meet obligations to the old party's staff.
A top social democrat, deputy parliament speaker Marek Borowski, said his party had no significant fortune left and relied on contributions from supporters.
"The whole campaign is just political cheek," he said.
